feedback: No race has yet been run on this geometry, so nothing here states its outcome. The evidence available is iteration 0, the baseline (wheel_track 0.12, radius 0.03, mass 0.7, sensors at y=0.06 spanning ±0.04 m). It finished 3 of 60 trials, all on the oval. The s-bend ended off-track with progress 0.24 and the slalom with progress 0.11, each with about one line-loss event per run and rms_error near 0.025. That suggests turn authority and reaction lag, not noise. To work with your narrower track, I kept sensor weights proportional to x and held kp at 2.5, added kd to damp the forward-offset lag, and raised base_speed. Next race decisions: if line_loss_events stay at 1 or more on the s-bend while progress stays near 0.25, the sensor span is too narrow for the tape edge, so widen x to about ±0.04 m at the same y. If steering_oscillation is high on the slalom while max_error is low, the forward offset is adding lag, so move y back toward 0.06 m. If the robot now finishes but completion_time is above 3 s, keep the 0.10 m track and mass near 0.6 kg, and raise base_speed further if the robot does not leave the track.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events is still at or above 1 on the s-bend while progress stays near 0.25 (iteration 0 baseline), widen the sensor x span to about ±0.04 m at y=0.07, keeping 5 sensors, so the summed reading stays above 0.05 at the tape edge.
If steering_oscillation is high on the slalom while max_error stays low (iteration 0 slalom max_error 0.064), move the sensor y back from 0.07 toward 0.06 m to reduce forward-offset lag.

If the robot finishes the oval but completion_time stays above 3 s, keep wheel_track at 0.10 m and reduce mass toward 0.5 kg, since the iteration 0 baseline mean finish time on the oval was 1.77 s and the target is under 3 s on every track.
